summary: The narrator, while working on a film shoot in New York in the rain, is confronted by a menacing man with a shoulder holster and a snub-nosed pistol who objects to what he is doing. The narrator, scared and shaking, calls 911 and threatens to report the man to the police, after which the man walks away and seems to vanish, possibly into a long black car heading toward Broadway. The narrator tells his assistant Arlene to watch for strangers but does not mention the gun, and is left puzzled about why anyone would be so worried about the shoot.
one_line: A film-shoot crew in rainy New York is confronted by a gun-carrying man who objects to the production, prompting the narrator to call 911.
key_facts: The narrator's new Hispanic friend abruptly drew up when he saw the cordial tete-a-tete being about to be disrupted.
The man wore a shoulder holster under his jacket containing a snub-nosed pistol.
The narrator thought the man's gun was not a prop.
The man's eyes were described as dead and merciless as he bored in on the narrator.
The man said to the narrator: "I think you are lying."
The man said: "That is a big mistake."
The narrator was scared, with hand shaking, and dialed 911 on his cell phone.
The narrator told the man: "Listen, if you're threatening me with a gun, I'm calling the cops."
The man abruptly turned and strode away as the New York police emergency number was still ringing.
The man seemed to disappear into the rain, though someone who could have been him got into a long black car down the block and sped toward Broadway.
The narrator thought Nicky Russo operated by an age-old set of Sicilian rules, unlike this man, whom he judged not to be the rule-book type.
Arlene said the man looked like a heavy in one of David's old action pictures and that all he needed was a Mack-10.
The narrator did not mention the gun to Arlene so as not to spook her.
The narrator could not think of any serious reason why anyone would be so worried about what he was doing.
